items.slavonic_text: Мꙋ́чениченъ: Что́ вы нарече́мъ ст҃і́и; * Херꙋві́мы ли; ꙗ҆́кѡ на ва́съ почи́лъ є҆́сть Хрⷭ҇то́съ, * Серафі́мы ли; ꙗ҆́кѡ непреста́ннѡ просла́висте є҆го̀, * А҆́гг҃лы ли; тѣ́ла бо ѿврати́стесѧ, * Си̑лы ли; дѣ́йствꙋете бо чꙋдесы̀, * мнѡ́гаѧ ва́ша и҆мена̀, и҆ бѡ́льшаѧ дарова́нїа, * моли́те спасти́сѧ дꙋша́мъ на́шымъ.
items.english_text: *Heirmos:* Ineffable is the Childbearing of a seedless conception, the incorrupt fruit of a husbandless Mother; for the birth of God renews nature; therefore, all generations, as the Bride of God and Mother, we orthodoxly magnify thee.

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Heirmos:*  
Ineffable is the Childbearing of a seedless conception, the incorrupt fruit of a husbandless Mother; for the birth of God renews nature; therefore, all generations, as the Bride of God and Mother, we orthodoxly magnify thee.

items.english_text: O Christ God, Who wast nailed to the Cross with robbers, and by Thy wound didst heal human nature, despise me not who have fallen into the hands of spiritual waylayers and bodiless robbers, and have been stripped by them of the robe of grace-given adoption, and lie with wounds as one lifeless; and the priest having come, seeing the wound, paid no heed; and the Levite also, abhorring it, passed by; but Thou, O Lord, Who wast ineffably incarnate of the Virgin, having poured forth from Thy saving side, which abundantly poured out blood and water, like oil dripping down, O Christ God, bind up the sores of my wounds with softness, and unite me unto the heavenly choir, as Thou art compassionate.[^1131]

items.english_text: What shall we call you, O saints? Cherubim? For Christ rested upon you. Seraphim? For unceasingly you glorified Him. Angels? For you turned away from the body. Powers? For you work miracles. Many are your names, and greater are your gifts; pray that our souls may be saved.

For you work miracles. Many are your names, and greater are your gifts; pray that our souls may be saved.

items.english_text: O marvelous wonder! O new mystery! O dreadful undertaking! The Virgin spoke, when she beheld Thee suspended upon the Cross between two robbers, Whom without pain she had wonderfully brought forth, weeping and saying: Woe is me, most beloved Child! How has a fierce and ungrateful people nailed Thee to the Cross?

How has a fierce and ungrateful people nailed Thee to the Cross?

items.english_text: Thus says the Lord God, the Holy One of Israel, Who made the things that are to come: Ask Me concerning My sons and concerning My daughters, and command Me concerning the works of My hands. [12] I made the earth and man upon it; I by My hand established heaven; I commanded all the stars. [13] I have raised him up with righteousness as king, and all his ways are right. He shall build My city, and he shall turn back the captivity of My people, not for price nor for reward, says the Lord of Sabaoth. [14] Thus says the Lord of Sabaoth: Egypt has labored, and the merchandise of the Ethiopians, and the Sabaeans, men of tall stature, shall come over unto thee, and they shall be thy servants; and they shall follow after thee, bound with hand-chains, and they shall pass over unto thee, and they shall bow down unto thee, and in thee shall they pray, for God is in thee, and they shall say: There is no God besides thee. [15] For Thou art God, and we knew it not, the God of Israel, the Savior. [16] All that oppose Him shall be ashamed and confounded, and they shall walk in shame; be renewed unto Me, O islands. [17] Israel is saved by the Lord with an everlasting salvation; they shall not be ashamed, neither shall they be confounded unto the age anymore, says the Lord.

items.english_text: As I went forth from the Jerusalem of Thy divine commandments, and arrived at the passions of Jericho, drawn by the glory of dishonor of worldly cares, I fell among robber-like thoughts, and was stripped by them of the robe of grace-given adoption, and lie with wounds as one lifeless; and the priest having come, seeing the wound, paid no heed; and the Levite also, abhorring it, passed by; but Thou, O Lord, Who wast ineffably incarnate of the Virgin, having poured forth from Thy saving side, which abundantly poured out blood and water, like oil dripping down, O Christ God, bind up the sores of my wounds with softness, and unite me unto the heavenly choir, as Thou art compassionate.[^1133]

items.english_text: Thou appearest unto me as a man, says the undefiled Maiden unto the Archistrategos, and how dost thou proclaim words surpassing man? For thou saidst that God shall be with me, and shall dwell in my womb; and how shall I be, tell me, a spacious domain and place of sanctification for Him Who surpasses the Cherubim? Deceive me not with guile, for I have not known pleasure, I am a stranger to marriage; how then shall I bring forth a Child?

items.english_text: The mystery hidden from the ages is revealed today, and the Son of God becomes the Son of Man, that taking the worse, He may impart unto me the better. Adam of old was deceived, and desiring to become God, he became not so; God becomes man, that He may make Adam god. Let creation rejoice, let nature dance, for the Archangel stands with fear before the Virgin, and brings the "Rejoice," the counter-weight to sorrow. O our God, Who in Thy tender mercy wast made man, glory to Thee![^1134]

items.english_text: And it came to pass after these words, that God tempted Abraham, and said unto him: Abraham, Abraham! And he said: Behold, here am I. [3] And Abraham rose up early in the morning, saddled his donkey, and took with him two of his servants, and Isaac his son; and having split wood for a whole-burnt offering, he arose and went, and came to the place of which God had told him, on the third day. [4] And Abraham, lifting up his eyes, saw the place afar off. [5] And Abraham said unto his servants: Sit ye here with the donkey; and I and the lad will go yonder, and having worshipped, we will return unto you. [6] And Abraham took the wood of the whole-burnt offering, and laid it upon Isaac his son; and he took in his hands both fire and the knife, and they went both of them together. [7] And Isaac spoke unto Abraham his father, and said: Father! And he said: What is it, my child? And he said: Behold the fire and the wood; where is the sheep for a whole-burnt offering? [8] And Abraham said: God will provide for Himself a sheep for a whole-burnt offering, my child. And having gone both of them together, [9] they came unto the place of which God had told him; and there Abraham built an altar, and laid the wood in order; and having bound Isaac his son, he laid him upon the altar on top of the wood. [12] And he said: Lay not thine hand upon the lad, neither do thou anything unto him; for now I know that thou fearest God, and hast not spared thy beloved son for My sake. items.preceding_stichos: Verse:* Bless the Lord, O my soul; O Lord my God, Thou hast been magnified exceedingly.
items.english_text: Brethren should be helpful in distress; for unto this end are they born. [18] A foolish man claps his hands and rejoices in himself, as he who gives surety also makes his friend surety; [19] and upon his lips he treasures up fire. [20] A lover of sin rejoices in quarrels, and the hard-hearted shall not meet with good things. [21] A man fickle of tongue shall fall into evils; and the heart of a fool is sorrow to him that has gotten him. [22] A father rejoices not over an undisciplined son; but a wise son brings joy to his mother. [23] A cheerful heart brings well-being; but the bones of a sorrowful man dry up. [24] The paths of him that receives unjust gifts in the bosom do not prosper; and the ungodly man perverts the ways of righteousness. [25] The face of a prudent man is wise, but the eyes of a fool are on the ends of the earth. [26] A foolish son is wrath unto his father, and grief unto her that bore him. [27] It is not good to lay fines upon a righteous man, neither is it holy to plot against righteous rulers. [28] He that spares to utter a harsh word is understanding; and a long-suffering man is very wise, better than he that seeks instruction. [29] Unto a senseless man asking for wisdom, wisdom shall be imputed; and he that keeps silent shall be deemed to be prudent. [18:1] A man seeking to separate from friends seeks pretexts; and at all times he shall be reproached. [2] A man void of understanding has no need of wisdom, for he is rather led by folly. [3] When an ungodly man comes into the depth of evils, he cares not; and dishonor and reproach come upon him. [4] The word in a man's heart is deep water, and a leaping river and fountain of life. [5] To accept the person of the ungodly is not good, neither is it holy to turn aside the righteous in judgment.

items.english_text: On this day we celebrate the Akathist Hymn of our Most Holy Lady Theotokos, for the following reason:[^1149] While Heraclius was ruling the imperial realm of the Greeks, Khosrow, the Persian king, seeing the Greek scepter brought low by Phocas the tyrant emperor, sent one of his grandees named Sarbaros with many thousands of troops to subjugate all the eastern lands unto himself; for Khosrow had previously destroyed ten times ten thousand Christians, selling them to the Jews who bought them and put them to death. The chief grandee Sarbaros, having conquered all the East, reached even to the Golden City, which is now called Scutari. Emperor Heraclius, having become impoverished in gold, converted the sacred church vessels into gold coins with the promise to return them in greater and more complete measure; and sailing through the Black Sea with ships to the Persian lands, he laid them waste. Khosrow was utterly defeated by him along with his remaining troops; and Siroes, Khosrow's son, learning of this, rebelled against his father, seized the rule for himself, slew his father Khosrow, and formed an alliance with Emperor Heraclius. But the Chagan of Mysia and ruler of the Scythians, learning that the emperor had departed across the Pontic Sea, broke the peace with the Greeks, moved countless legions, and came from the western parts against Constantinople, crying out blasphemous words against God. Immediately the sea was filled with ships, and the land was full of countless foot-soldiers and horsemen. But Sergius, the Patriarch of Constantinople, greatly comforted the people, urging them not to lose heart or weaken, but from their soul to place all their hope in God and in His most pure Mother, the Theotokos. Likewise Bonus the Patrician, who was then governing the city, prepared what was needed to equip the warriors; for it behooves us also, with help from on high, to act fittingly. The Patriarch, bearing the divine icons of the Mother of God, along with the whole multitude, went in procession along the walls from above, giving them courage from thence. For while Sarbaros from the east and the Chagan from the west were advancing to burn the environs of the city, the Patriarch went along the walls carrying the Icon of Christ Not-Made-by-Hands, the precious and life-creating Wood of the Cross, and the venerable Robe of the Mother of God. The Chagan, a Scythian, attacked the walls of Constantinople by land with an innumerable multitude, fortified with strong siege weapons; and so great was their number that one Greek had to fight against ten Scythians. But the invincible Champion, through the few soldiers who were near Her church called Pigi [the Spring], destroyed the greater part of them. Hence the Greeks, taking courage and rejoicing, by the aid of their unconquerable Leader, the Mother of God, continually defeated them unto the end. And when the citizens looked toward reconciliation, they were rejected; for the Chagan answered them: "Be not deceived in the God in Whom you believe, for tomorrow by all means I shall take your city." Hearing this, the citizens stretched out their hands unto God. The Chagan and Sarbaros having agreed together, attacked the city by land and sea, seeking to work destruction by their wiles; but they were so defeated by the Greeks that the living were not sufficient to burn the dead. And their monoxyla [canoes], filled with armed men, in the gulf called the Golden Horn, near the church of the Mother of God at Blachernae, were suddenly struck by a violent tempest that fell upon the sea and tore it asunder, so that all the ships of the enemies were scattered. And one could see that most glorious and marvelous sight of the Most Pure Mother of God: all were cast upon the seashore at Blachernae. The people quickly opened the gates and slew them all together, and even the children and women fell upon them. Their commanders returned weeping and wailing together. Therefore the God-loving people of Constantinople, rendering thanks unto the Mother of God, rendering thanks, sang unto Her an all-night and unseated song [the Akathist], as unto Her who had kept vigil over them and by supernatural power had wrought victory over their enemies. From that time forth, in remembrance of so great and supernatural a wonder, the Church received this feast, to offer it unto the Mother of God at this present season, wherein the victory also was won by the Mother of God. And it was called "unseated" [Akathistos] because the city choir and all the people then stood upright while singing it.[^1150]

provenance.verbatim_source: On this day we celebrate the Akathist Hymn of our Most Holy Lady Theotokos, for the following reason:[^1149] While Heraclius was ruling the imperial realm of the Greeks, Khosrow, the Persian king, seeing the Greek scepter brought low by Phocas the tyrant emperor, sent one of his grandees named Sarbaros with many thousands of troops to subjugate all the eastern lands unto himself; for Khosrow had previously destroyed ten times ten thousand Christians, selling them to the Jews who bought them and put them to death. The chief grandee Sarbaros, having conquered all the East, reached even to the Golden City, which is now called Scutari. Emperor Heraclius, having become impoverished in gold, converted the sacred church vessels into gold coins with the promise to return them in greater and more complete measure; and sailing through the Black Sea with ships to the Persian lands, he laid them waste. Khosrow was utterly defeated by him along with his remaining troops; and Siroes, Khosrow's son, learning of this, rebelled against his father, seized the rule for himself, slew his father Khosrow, and formed an alliance with Emperor Heraclius. items.english_text: After the passage of thirty-six years, in the reign of Constantine Pogonatus, the Hagarenes, leading a countless army, attacked Constantinople again; and warring against it for seven years, during which they wintered in the regions of Cyzicus, they lost many of their men. Then, giving up the war and returning with their army, when they were near the sea called Syllaeum, they were all drowned through the intercession of the most pure Mother of God.

items.english_text: And yet a third time, under Leo the Isaurian, the Hagarenes, in numbers far exceeding the former, first laid waste the Persian kingdom, then Egypt and Libya; and having overrun India, Ethiopia, and Spain, finally they waged war against the Imperial City itself, borne upon one thousand eight hundred ships. Having encircled it, they expected immediately to plunder it. But the sacred citizens, bearing about the precious Wood of the venerable and life-creating Cross and the venerable icon of the Mother of God Hodigitria, circled the wall, propitiating God with tears. Then it seemed good to the Hagarenes to divide themselves into two parts: some made war against the Bulgarians and there fell more than twenty thousand; while the others remained to take Constantinople, but were prevented by the chain that stretched from Galata unto the walls of the Imperial City. Having sailed up as far as a place called Sosthenes, there a north wind blew upon them, and many of their ships were shattered and destroyed; and those who remained fell into severe famine, so that they even tasted human flesh and kneaded dung and ate it. Then fleeing, when they reached the Aegean deep, all their light vessels and they themselves were delivered unto the depth of the sea; for a violent hailstorm fell from heaven, stirring up the sea, and melted the pitch of the ships. And so that countless multitude of ships perished, only three remaining to bring the tidings.

items.english_text: For the sake of all these supernatural wonders of the All-Pure Mother of God, we celebrate the present feast. And it was called "unseated" because all the people, standing upright on that night, sang the hymn unto the Mother of the Word; and whereas it is customary to sit during all others, during these hymns of the Mother of God we all listen standing upright.

items.slavonic_text: Тебѐ ᲂу҆́бѡ возбрана́ше, честны́хъ взира́нїа, скве́рнъ пре́жде привлече́нное скверне́нїе: * твое́ же чꙋ́вство, и҆ твоѧ̀ бг҃омꙋ́драѧ содѣ́ѧнныхъ совѣ́сть, къ лꙋ́чшымъ тебѐ ѡ҆браще́нїе содѣ́лаша, * на І҆кѡ́нꙋ бо воззрѣ́вши бл҃гослове́нныѧ Бг҃оѻтрокови́цы, * всѣ́хъ пока́ѧвшисѧ прегрѣше́нїй свои́хъ, всехва́льнаѧ пре́жнихъ, * въ дерзнове́нїи честно́мꙋ Дре́вꙋ поклони́ласѧ є҆сѝ.
items.english_text: The pollution of past defilements held thee back from beholding the precious sights; but thy perception and thy God-wise conscience concerning what had been committed wrought thy turning unto better things. For looking upon the Icon of the blessed Maiden of God, having repented of all thy former transgressions, O all-lauded one, with boldness thou didst venerate the precious Wood.

provenance.verbatim_source: The pollution of past defilements held thee back from beholding the precious sights; but thy perception and thy God-wise conscience concerning what had been committed wrought thy turning unto better things. items.slavonic_text: Мѣ́стѡмъ поклони́вшисѧ, ра́достїю ст҃ы̑мъ, * добродѣ́тели напꙋ́тное спаси́тельнѣйшее, ѿтꙋ́дꙋ прїѧ́ла є҆сѝ, * и҆ ѕѣлѡ̀ потекла̀ є҆сѝ до́брое ше́ствїе: * и҆ стрꙋ́ю преше́дши І҆ѻрда́нскꙋю, въ жили́ще Предте́чево, ᲂу҆се́рднѡ всели́ласѧ є҆сѝ, * и҆ страсте́й свирѣ́пство, жи́тельствомъ ѡ҆мрачи́ла є҆сѝ, * и҆стончава́ющи въ дерзнове́нїи, приснопа́мѧтнаѧ Мт҃и, плотска̑ѧ сво́йства.
items.english_text: Having with joy venerated the holy places, from thence thou didst receive the most saving viaticum of virtue, and didst run exceedingly well on thy noble journey. And crossing the stream of the Jordan, thou didst eagerly dwell in the habitation of the Forerunner, and by thy way of life didst darken the fierceness of the passions, boldly refining away, O ever-memorable mother, the properties of the flesh.

items.slavonic_text: Въ пꙋсты́ню всели́вшисѧ, твои́хъ страсте́й ѻ҆́бразы, ѿ дꙋшѝ ѿѧ́ла є҆сѝ, * бг҃ови́днѣйшее и҆зѡбраже́нїе въ дꙋшѝ написа́вши, добродѣ́телей ви́ды: * и҆ толи́кѡ просїѧ́ла є҆сѝ, ꙗ҆́кѡ и҆ вода́ми легкѡ̀ преходи́ти бл҃же́ннаѧ, * и҆ ѿ землѝ взима́тисѧ, въ твои́хъ къ Бг҃ꙋ моле́нїихъ: * и҆ ны́нѣ въ дерзнове́нїи всесла́внаѧ Марї́е, * Хрⷭтꙋ̀ предстоя́щи, моли́сѧ ѡ҆ дꙋша́хъ на́шихъ.
items.english_text: Having settled in the wilderness, thou didst banish from thy soul the images of thy passions, inscribing upon thy soul the most Godlike depiction: the forms of virtues. And so greatly didst thou shine forth, O blessed one, that thou didst even walk lightly over the waters, and was lifted up from the earth in thy supplications unto God. And now, O all-glorious Mary, standing before Christ with boldness, pray for our souls!

items.english_text: *Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "The Wisdom and the Word" (Премꙋ́дрость и҆ Сло́во):* Having bridled all the surges of the flesh by ascetic labors, thou didst show forth the courageous disposition of thy soul; for longing to behold the Cross of the Lord, O all-honorable one, thou didst crucify thyself unto the world. items.english_text: *Kontakion, Tone 3, Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дѣ́ва дне́сь):* Though formerly filled with all manner of defilement, today through repentance she is shown forth as the Bride of Christ; imitating the angelic way of life, she destroys the demons with the weapon of the Cross; for this cause hast thou been revealed as a Bride of the Kingdom, O Mary all-glorious!

provenance.verbatim_source:

Though formerly filled with all manner of defilement, today through repentance she is shown forth as the Bride of Christ; imitating the angelic way of life, she destroys the demons with the weapon of the Cross; for this cause hast thou been revealed as a Bride of the Kingdom, O Mary all-glorious!

items.english_text: *Ikos:* The ewe-lamb and daughter of Christ let us praise now in hymns, the ever-memorable Mary, who appeared as a lamb from Egypt, and having escaped from all their delusion, she alone was offered to the Church as a perfect growth, striving through abstinence and prayer beyond the measure of human nature; therefore the one Sovereign Ruler exalted the life and deeds of Mary all-glorious!

items.english_text: Thou Who searchest the depths of the heart, Who foreknowest all that is ours before being: Thou didst snatch away from the violent life her who fled unto Thee, O Savior, who urgently and unceasingly cries unto Thy love for mankind: Ye priests, bless; ye people, supremely exalt unto all ages!

items.english_text: O the honorable change, the turning of thyself unto that which is better, O honorable one! O divine love, which hated carnal pleasures! O fervent and divine faith, O all-lauded Mary! Whom we faithfully praise and supremely exalt unto the ages!

items.english_text: Rich and unmerciful, in my mind I have despised Thy commandments through lack of faith, O Lover of mankind, being cast down grievously before the gates; but as Thou art compassionate and overflowing in mercy, raise me up, even as of old Thou didst raise Lazarus, Thy friend of four days!

items.english_text: The Kingdom of God is not food and drink, but righteousness and abstinence with holiness; therefore neither shall the rich enter into it, but those who place their treasures into the hands of the poor. These things David the prophet also teaches, saying: Righteous is the man that is merciful all the day long, who delights in the Lord and walking in the light he will not stumble; all these things were written for our instruction, that while fasting we may practice kindness, and the Lord will give us heavenly things instead of earthly!

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.english_text: Having become poor, O Christ, Thou rich One, Thou didst enrich men with immortality and radiance; therefore, enrich me who have become impoverished by the pleasures of life with virtues, and join me unto Lazarus the poor, delivering me from the torment of the rich man and from the Gehenna that lies before me!

items.english_text: I have become grievously rich in wickedness, and have loved sweetness, and have enjoyed the pleasures of this life, O Lord, and I am condemned to the fire of Gehenna; wasting away in mind from hunger, cast down before the gates of divine deeds, like Lazarus despised, have compassion upon me, O Master!

items.english_text: *Another Sticheron, in the same Tone, Podoben: "A radiant cloud" (Ѻ҆́блакъ тѧ̀):*[^1166] Eagerly beginning the sixth week of the venerable Fasts, let us, the faithful, offer unto the Lord a prefestal hymn of the Palms, as He comes in glory by the power of His Divinity to Jerusalem to put death to death; let us therefore piously prepare the emblems of victory, the branches of virtues, crying aloud: "Hosanna" unto the Creator of all!

items.english_text: Marvelous is the Savior's disposition of love toward mankind for our sake: possessing the knowledge of things to come as though present, He set forth the life of Lazarus and of the rich man; contemplating the end of both, let us flee the unmercifulness and inhumanity of the one, and let us emulate the patience and greatness of soul of the other, so that, being comforted with him in the bosom of Abraham, we may cry aloud: O righteous Judge, O Lord, glory to Thee!

items.english_text: Thou didst roll away the stone of callousness, O Lord, from my heart; raise up my soul put to death by passions, O Good One, to offer Thee the palms of virtues as unto the Conqueror of Hades; make me worthy of compunction, O Master, that I may obtain eternal life, hymning Thy dominion and Thy compassion, O only Lover of mankind! *(Twice)*

items.slavonic_text: Шестꙋ́ю седми́цꙋ поста̀ и҆мꙋ́ще, предпра́зднственное пѣ́нїе, * ва́їа принесе́мъ Хрⷭ҇тꙋ̀, * грѧдꙋ́щему на́съ ра́ди всѣ́сти на жребѧ́ти ѻ҆́сли, * ꙗ҆зы́ческое подклони́ти ꙗ҆́кѡ Цр҃ь безслове́сїе Роди́телю, * вѣ́тви добродѣ́телей томꙋ̀ всѝ ᲂу҆гото́вимъ, * ꙗ҆́кѡ да Воскрⷭ҇нїе є҆гѡ̀ ра́дꙋющесѧ ᲂу҆́зримъ.
items.english_text: Holding the sixth week of the Fast, let us offer unto Christ a prefestal hymn, palms, as He comes for our sake to sit upon the foal of an ass, to subdue the irrationality of the Gentiles as King unto the Father; let us all prepare for Him the branches of virtues, that rejoicing we may behold His Resurrection!

provenance.verbatim_source: Holding the sixth week of the Fast, let us offer unto Christ a prefestal hymn, palms, as He comes for our sake to sit upon the foal of an ass, to subdue the irrationality of the Gentiles as King unto the Father; let us all prepare for Him the branches of virtues, that rejoicing we may behold His Resurrection!

items.slavonic_text: Рꙋ́цѣ твоѝ бж҃твеннїи, и҆́миже Содѣ́телѧ носи́ла є҆сѝ, * Дв҃о прест҃а́ѧ, воплоще́нна Бж҃ество́мъ, * просте́рши ᲂу҆молѝ, и҆зба́витисѧ на́мъ ѿ и҆скꙋше́нїй, * и҆ страсте́й, и҆ бѣ́дъ, восхвалѧ́ющимъ тѧ̀ любо́вїю, * и҆ вопїю́щымъ тебѣ̀: * сла́ва Все́льшемꙋсѧ въ тѧ̀: * сла́ва Проше́дшемꙋ и҆з̾ тебѐ: * сла́ва Свободи́вшемꙋ на́съ Ржⷭ҇тво́мъ твои́мъ.
items.english_text: Having stretched forth thy divine hands, wherewith thou didst bear the Creator, O All-Holy Virgin, incarnate in His Divinity, pray that we may be delivered from temptations, passions, and tribulations, who praise thee with love, crying aloud unto thee: Glory to Him Who dwelt within thee! Glory to Him Who came forth from thee! Glory to Him Who delivered us by thy Childbirth!

items.english_text: *Troparion:* Let us put to death the passions by abstinence, and let us bring the spirit to life by divine deeds, that with a pure mind we may behold the precious Passion of Christ!

items.slavonic_text: Неми́лостивагѡ поревнова́вша, бога́тагѡ нра́вѡмъ, * Ще́дре Человѣколю́бче молю́ тѧ, * сочинѝ мѧ Ла́зарю ᲂу҆бо́гомꙋ, * и҆збавлѧ́ѧ мѧ̀ пла́мене и҆ негаси́магѡ ѻ҆гнѧ̀.
items.english_text: Emulating the disposition of the unmerciful rich man, I pray Thee, O Compassionate One, Lover of mankind: reckon me with Lazarus the poor, delivering me from the flame and unquenchable fire!

provenance.verbatim_source: Emulating the disposition of the unmerciful rich man, I pray Thee, O Compassionate One, Lover of mankind: reckon me with Lazarus the poor, delivering me from the flame and unquenchable fire!

items.english_text: I have fasted from all good deeds, and have taken my fill of transgressions, O Lord; therefore, now satisfy me who hunger with saving and precious food!

items.english_text: *Theotokion:* O All-Pure Mistress, who didst bear the all-compassionate God: save and have compassion upon me who am condemned in condemnation, cast down by my deeds!

provenance.verbatim_source:

items.english_text: Appropriately keeping the Forefeast of the Flower-bearing feast brightly today, O ye faithful, let us be accounted worthy to behold the life-bearing Passion!

provenance.verbatim_source: Appropriately keeping the Forefeast of the Flower-bearing feast brightly today, O ye faithful, let us be accounted worthy to behold the life-bearing Passion!

items.english_text: Christ advances and comes unto Jerusalem as King, sitting upon the foal of an ass, to subdue the irrationality of the Gentiles beneath the yoke of the Father!

items.english_text: O Three-Hypostatic Unity in one Godhead, Unbegotten Father, God, and Only-Begotten Son, and One Holy Spirit, Consubstantial Dominion: save us all!

provenance.verbatim_source: O Three-Hypostatic Unity in one Godhead, Unbegotten Father, God, and Only-Begotten Son, and One Holy Spirit, Consubstantial Dominion: save us all!

items.slavonic_text: === LEAF p422 === (Printed Folio 418) Їрмо́съ: Помо́гшемꙋ Бг҃ꙋ во Є҆гѵ́птѣ Мѡѷсе́и, и҆ тѣ́мъ фараѡ́на со всево́инствомъ погрꙋзи́вшемꙋ, * побѣ́днꙋю пѣ́снь пои́мъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ просла́висѧ.
items.english_text: Most glorious things were spoken concerning thee everywhere, for in the flesh thou didst bear the Creator of all, O Mary Theotokos, unwedded and knowing not wedlock!

items.english_text: Behold, Christ comes unto the village of Bethphage; rejoice, O Bethany, homeland of Lazarus, for unto thee shall He show a great wonder, raising Lazarus from the dead!

items.english_text: Thus says the Lord, Who delivered thee, the Holy One of Israel: I am the Lord thy God, Who taught thee that thou shouldst find the way wherein thou shouldst walk. And if thou hadst listened to My commandments, then would thy peace have been as a river, and thy righteousness as a wave of the sea. And thy seed would have been as the sand, and the offspring of thy womb as the dust of the earth; neither now shalt thou be utterly destroyed, nor shall thy name perish before Me. Go forth from Babylon, flee from the Chaldeans; proclaim with a voice of joy, and let this be heard, proclaim it even unto the ends of the earth; say: The Lord has redeemed His servant Jacob! And if they thirst, He will lead them through the wilderness, and bring forth water out of the rock for them; the rock shall be cleft, and the water shall flow, and My people shall drink. There is no joy for the ungodly, says the Lord.

items.english_text: And it came to pass after Isaac was old, that his eyes were dimmed so that he could not see; and he called Esau his elder son, and said unto him: My son! And he said: Behold, here am I. And Isaac said: Behold, I am old, and I know not the day of my end. Now therefore take thy weapons, thy quiver and thy bow, and go out into the field, and hunt game for me. And make me savory meat, such as I love, and bring it to me, that I may eat; so that my soul may bless thee before I die. And Rebekah heard Isaac speaking to Esau his son. And Esau went to the field to hunt game for his father. And Rebekah spoke unto Jacob unto her younger son, saying: Behold, I heard thy father speaking unto Esau thy brother, saying: Bring me game, and make me savory meat, that I may eat, and bless thee before the Lord, before my death. Now therefore, my son, obey my voice according to what I command thee. Go now to the flock, and fetch me from thence two tender and good kids of the goats; and I will make them savory meat for thy father, such as he loves. And thou shalt bring it to thy father, that he may eat, so that thy father may bless thee before his death. And Jacob said to Rebekah his mother: Behold, Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man. What if my father feel me, and I seem unto him as a deceiver, and I bring a curse upon myself, and not a blessing? And his mother said unto him: Upon me be thy curse, my son; only obey my voice, and go fetch them to me. And he went, and fetched them, and brought them to his mother; and his mother made savory meat, such as his father loved. And Rebekah took the goodly raiment of her eldest son Esau, which was with her in the house, and put it upon Jacob her younger son. And she put the skins of the kids of the goats upon his hands, and upon the smooth of his neck. And she gave the savory meat and the bread, which she had prepared, into the hands of her son Jacob.

items.english_text: And he came unto his father, and said: My father! And he said: Here am I; who art thou, my son? And Jacob said unto his father: I am Esau thy firstborn; I have done according as thou badest me: arise, sit and eat of my game, that thy soul may bless me. And Isaac said unto his son: How is it that thou hast found it so quickly, my son? And he said: Because the Lord thy God brought it before me. And Isaac said unto Jacob: Come near, I pray thee, that I may feel thee, my son, whether thou be my son Esau or not. And Jacob went near unto Isaac his father; and he felt him, and said: The voice indeed is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau. And he discerned him not, because his hands were hairy, as his brother Esau's hands: so he blessed him. And he said: Art thou my son Esau? And he said: I am. And he said: Bring it near to me, and I will eat of my son's game, that my soul may bless thee. And he brought it near to him, and he did eat; and he brought him wine, and he drank. And his father Isaac said unto him: Come near now, and kiss me, my son. And he came near, and kissed him; and he smelled the smell of his raiment, and blessed him, and said: See, the smell of my son is as the smell of a full field which the Lord hath blessed! And may God give thee of the dew of heaven, and of the fatness of the earth, and plenty of corn and wine; and let nations serve thee, and princes bow down to thee; be lord over thy brother, and let thy father's sons bow down to thee: cursed be everyone that curses thee, and blessed be he that blesses thee!

items.english_text: And it came to pass, as soon as Isaac had made an end of blessing Jacob his son, and Jacob was scarcely gone out from the presence of Isaac his father, that Esau his brother came in from his hunting. And he also had made savory meat, and brought it unto his father, and said unto his father: Let my father arise, and eat of his son's game, that thy soul may bless me. And Isaac his father said unto him: Who art thou? And he said: I am thy son, thy firstborn, Esau. And Isaac trembled with an exceedingly great trembling, and said: Who then was he that took game and brought it to me, and I have eaten of all before thou camest, and have blessed him? Yea, and he shall be blessed! And when Esau heard the words of his father Isaac, he cried with a great and exceeding bitter cry, and said: Bless me, even me also, O my father! And he said: Thy brother came with subtilty, and hath taken away thy blessing. And Esau said: Is he not rightly named Jacob? For he hath supplanted me these two times: he took away my birthright, and, behold, now he hath taken away my blessing. And Esau said unto his father: Hast thou not reserved a blessing for me, O my father? And Isaac answered and said unto Esau: Behold, I have made him thy master, and all his brethren have I given to him for servants; and with corn and wine have I sustained him: and what shall I do now unto thee, my son? And Esau said unto his father: Hast thou but one blessing, my father? Bless me, even me also, O my father! And Isaac was moved with compassion, and Esau lifted up his voice, and wept. And Isaac his father answered and said unto him: Behold of the fatness of the earth shall be thy dwelling, and of the dew of heaven from above; and by thy sword shalt thou live, and shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt cast down and break loose his yoke from thy neck. And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him.

And he also had made savory meat, and brought it unto his father, and said unto his father: Let my father arise, and eat of his son's game, that thy soul may bless me. And Isaac his father said unto him: Who art thou? And he said: I am thy son, thy firstborn, Esau. And Isaac trembled with an exceedingly great trembling, and said: Who then was he that took game and brought it to me, and I have eaten of all before thou camest, and have blessed him? Yea, and he shall be blessed! And when Esau heard the words of his father Isaac, he cried with a great and exceeding bitter cry, and said: Bless me, even me also, O my father! And he said: Thy brother came with subtilty, and hath taken away thy blessing. And Esau said: Is he not rightly named Jacob? For he hath supplanted me these two times: he took away my birthright, and, behold, now he hath taken away my blessing. items.english_text: He that keeps the commandment keeps his soul; but he that despises his ways shall die. He that has mercy on the poor lends unto the Lord, and according to his gift it shall be repaid unto him. Chasten thy son, for so shall he be of good hope, and let not thy soul be stirred up unto reproach. A man of great wrath shall suffer punishment; and if he do harm, he shall add yet more to it. Listen, my son, to the instruction of thy father, that thou mayest be wise in thy latter end. There are many devices in the heart of a man; but the counsel of the Lord endures forever. The fruit of a man is his mercy, and a poor righteous man is better than a rich liar. The fear of the Lord is unto life for a man; but he that is without fear shall abide in places where there is no discretion. He that hides his hands in his bosom unjustly will not so much as bring them to his mouth. When a pestilent man is scourged, a simple man becomes more prudent; and if thou reprove a man of understanding, he will understand knowledge.

items.slavonic_text: Па́че ᲂу҆ма̀ ржⷭ҇тво̀ твоѐ Бг҃ома́ти, * без̾ мꙋ́жа бо зача́тїе въ тебѣ̀, * и҆ дѣ́вственное ржⷭ҇тво̀ бы́сть: * ꙗ҆́кѡ Бг҃ъ є҆́сть рожде́йсѧ, * є҆го́же велича́юще, тѧ̀ Дв҃о ᲂу҆блажа́емъ.
items.english_text: Beyond understanding is thy childbirth, O Mother of God, for without a man was the conception within thee, and virginal was the birth; for He Who was born is God, Whom magnifying, we call thee blessed, O Virgin!

provenance.verbatim_source: Beyond understanding is thy childbirth, O Mother of God, for without a man was the conception within thee, and virginal was the birth; for He Who was born is God, Whom magnifying, we call thee blessed, O Virgin!

items.slavonic_text: Прїиди́те, ᲂу҆гото́вимъ Гдⷭ҇ни къ срѣ́тенїю, * вѣ́тви добродѣ́телей носѧ́ще є҆мꙋ̀: * та́кѡ бо є҆го̀ прїи́мемъ, ꙗ҆́коже во гра́дѣ І҆ерл҃имѣ, * въ дꙋшѝ на́шей, покланѧ́ющесѧ и҆ пою́ще є҆го̀.
items.english_text: Come, let us prepare for the meeting of the Lord, carrying unto Him the branches of virtues; for thus shall we receive Him, as in the city of Jerusalem, into our soul, worshiping and singing praises unto Him!

items.slavonic_text: Свѣти́ленъ.
items.english_text: Having stumbled through transgressions and bound with the cords of sins, O my soul, why dost thou despair? Why art thou slothful? Flee ever, like Lot, from the conflagration of the impurity of Sodom and Gomorrah; turn not back, lest thou become as a pillar of salt; save thyself upon the mountain of virtues; flee ever from the unmerciful rich man's burning heartlessness; pass over into the bosom of Abraham like Lazarus, and in humility of mind cry aloud: My hope and my refuge, O Lord, glory to Thee!

items.slavonic_text: Поползнꙋ́вшисѧ прегрѣше́ньми, * и҆ плени́цами согрѣше́нїй свѧ́зана, ѽ дꙋшѐ, что̀ ᲂу҆ныва́еши; * что̀ лѣни́шисѧ; * бѣ́гай при́снѡ, ꙗ҆́коже Лѡ́тъ, Содо́мы и҆ Гомо́рры, нечистоты̀ запале́нїѧ, * не возвраща́йсѧ вспѧ́ть, и҆ бꙋ́деши ꙗ҆́кѡ сто́лпъ со́льный, * на горѣ̀ спаса́йсѧ добродѣ́телей, * бѣга́й при́снѡ немилосе́рднагѡ бога́тагѡ, безꙋтро́бїа горѣ́нїѧ, * въ нѣ́дра прейдѝ А҆враа́мова ꙗ҆́кѡ Ла́зарь, * смиреномꙋ́дрїемъ возопи́й: * ᲂу҆пова́нїе моѐ, и҆ прибѣ́жище моѐ, * Гдⷭ҇и сла́ва тебѣ̀.
items.english_text: Thy Passion-bearers, O Lord, having emulated the Angelic ranks, endured torments as though bodiless, having unanimous hope, the enjoyment of promised good things; by their supplications, O Christ our God, grant peace unto Thy world, and unto our souls great mercy!

items.english_text: Thus saith the Lord: Behold, I have given Thee for a covenant of the race, for a light of the Gentiles, that Thou mayest be for salvation unto the end of the earth. Thus saith the Lord, the God of Israel that delivered Thee: Sanctify Him that despises His own life, Him that is abominable unto the nations, the servant of princes; kings shall behold Him, and princes shall arise, and shall worship Him, for the Lord's sake, because the Holy One of Israel is faithful, and I have chosen Thee. Thus saith the Lord: In an acceptable time have I heard Thee, and in a day of salvation have I helped Thee, and formed Thee; and I have given Thee for an everlasting covenant of the nations, to establish the earth, and to inherit the desolate heritages; saying to them that are in bonds: Go forth! and to them that are in darkness: Show yourselves! They shall feed along all the ways, and their pasture shall be in all paths. They shall not hunger, neither shall they thirst, neither shall heat nor sun smite them; but He that hath mercy on them shall comfort them.

items.english_text: The Lord said unto Jacob: Return into the land of thy father, and to thy kindred, and I will be with thee. And Jacob sent and called Leah and Rachel to the field where the flocks were. And he said unto them: I see your father's face, that it is not toward me as yesterday and the third day; but the God of my father hath been with me. And ye yourselves know that with all my power I have served your father. And your father hath wronged me, and changed my wages of ten lambs; but God suffered him not to do me evil. If he said thus: The speckled shall be thy wages; then all the sheep bare speckled; and if he said: The white shall be thy wages; then all the sheep bare white. And God took away all the cattle of your father, and gave them to me. And it came to pass, when the sheep conceived in the womb, that I saw with mine eyes in a dream, and, behold, the rams and the he-goats that leaped upon the sheep and goats were streaked, speckled, and ash-colored spotted. And the Angel of God spake unto me in a dream, saying: Jacob! And I said: What is it? And He said: Lift up thine eyes, and behold the rams and the he-goats that leap upon the sheep and the goats, white, speckled, and ash-colored spotted; for I have seen all that Laban does unto thee. I am the God Who appeared unto thee in the place of God, where thou anointedst a pillar for Me, and where thou vowedst a vow unto Me; now therefore arise, and get thee out from this land, and go into the land of thy nativity, and I will be with thee. And Rachel and Leah answered and said unto him: Is there yet any portion or inheritance for us in our father's house? Were we not counted as strangers unto him? For he hath sold us, and hath quite devoured our silver. All the riches and the glory which God hath taken from our father, that shall be ours, and our children's; now then, whatsoever God hath said unto thee, do!

items.english_text: My son, to do what is righteous and to speak the truth is more pleasing to God than the blood of sacrifices. A haughty man is insolent of heart in his reproach; and the lamp of the wicked is sin. The thoughts of the diligent tend to abundance, but every slothful man is in want. He that gathers treasures with a lying tongue pursus vanity into the snares of death. Destruction shall fall upon the ungodly, for they refuse to do what is right. Unto the crooked God sends crooked paths, for pure and right are His works. It is better to dwell in a corner of an unroofed place than in plastered rooms with unrighteousness, and in a shared house. The soul of the wicked shall find no mercy from any man. When the intemperate man is penalized, the simple becomes wiser; and when the wise man is instructed he shall receive understanding. The righteous man understands the hearts of the ungodly, and despises the ungodly in their evils. Whoso stops his ears from hearing the weak, he also shall cry, and there shall be none to hear him. A secret gift turns away anger, but he that is sparing of gifts stirs up strong wrath. It is joy to the righteous to do judgment, but the holy man is an abomination unto evildoers. A man that wanders out of the way of righteousness shall rest in the congregation of the giants. A needy man loves mirth, and he that loves wine and oil shall not be rich. The lawless man is a ransom for the righteous. It is better to dwell in a wilderness than with a contentious, talkative, and passionate woman. A desirable treasure rests in the mouth of the wise, but foolish men swallow it down. The way of righteousness and mercy finds life and glory.

items.english_text: Clothed in the divinely woven purple robe of dominion and in the scarlet mantle of incorruption, O my soul, thou hast disgraced thy dignity, turning wealth and enjoyment into sin, and despising thy fellow kinsman, even as the rich man despised poor Lazarus; but lest thou be tormented with him, become poor in spirit, and cry aloud unto the Lord Who became poor for thy sake: O Christ, Who before Thy crucifixion wast arrayed in the purple robe of mockery, and for my sake wast crucified naked upon the Cross, by the vesture of Thy Kingdom deliver me from eternal shame!

For leaving behind corruptible things, ye received incorruptible, and dancing with the Angels, ye unceasingly sing praises unto the Consubstantial Trinity!

items.english_text: *Cross-Theotokion, Podoben: "Being the wellspring of loving-kindness" (Милосе́рдїа [сꙋ́щи]):* Preserved by the precious Cross of thy Son, O pure Lady Theotokos, we all easily repel every assault of the slanderer; therefore, as is our duty, we glorify thee as Mother of the Light and the only hope of our souls!

items.english_text: Today Lazarus, having died, is buried, and his kinsfolk sing a lamentation; as the Foreseer and God, Thou didst foretell the event, saying unto the disciples: Lazarus is fallen asleep, but now I go to raise up him whom I created; therefore we all cry aloud unto Thee: Glory to the dominion of Thy might! *(Twice)*

items.english_text: Having said that Thou wouldst go again into Judea, O Lord, Thou didst make the disciples afraid; but Thomas cried aloud with boldness: He is Life! Let us go, and even if we die, we shall straightway live!

items.english_text: Consubstantial Trinity, Almighty Father, co-unoriginate Son, with the enthroned divine Spirit, one worship, uncreated Godhead, we all, being mortal men, sing praises unto Thee!

items.english_text: O Virgin Mother all-pure, root of Jesse, from whom Christ shone forth, the life-bearing blossom of earthborn men, whereby we were delivered from death, we all sing praises unto thee, O Pure One!

items.english_text: Cutting branches of virtues as from the Mount of Olives, from the heights of almsgiving, come, O ye people, let us mentally prepare the coming of Christ unto us, singing, blessing Him, and supremely exalting Him unto all ages!

items.english_text: *Triadikon:* O Three-Hypostatic Unity, Father, Son, and living Spirit, one Godhead, one Kingdom, the angelic hosts of unsetting light praise Thee, and we of the earth sing, bless, and supremely exalt Thee unto all ages!

items.english_text: Behold, all generations call thee blessed, O All-Pure One, beholding thy great deeds; for beyond nature thou didst bring forth the Creator of all, Who is God and man; therefore we bless and supremely exalt thee unto the ages!

items.english_text: With the children let us also meet Christ our God, offering almsgiving instead of palms unto hearty prayer, crying aloud with branches: Hosanna! Bless and supremely exalt Him unto the ages!

items.day_or_date: On Wednesday of Palm Week, at Matins
items.english_text: O Word of God, having raised by Thy life-giving word my soul, which hath been put to death by sins and shut up in the tomb of transgression, account me worthy to offer unto Thee, the Conqueror of death, the branches of virtues!

items.english_text: Having heaven as a throne and the earth as a footstool, the Word of God the Father, borne upon a foal, comes into the Holy City, to perfect out of the mouths of babes fair praise, as King of all!

items.english_text: Again Christ comes unto thee, O Judea, murderer of men, desiring as God to fulfill the saving Passion; Whom thou didst seek to kill with stones, behold, He comes unto thee willingly, of His own accord, unto thy slaughter, in order to save us!

items.english_text: The Godhead is a Monad and a Trinity; O most glorious mystery! Being united in essence, It is divided by Persons, specifically; for being indivisible, It is divided, and being one, It is threefold; This is the Father, the Son, and the living Spirit, Which preserves all things!

items.day_or_date: On Wednesday of Palm Week, at Matins
items.english_text: Who hath heard of a childbearing Virgin, and a Mother without a husband? O Mary, thou workest a wonder! But tell me, how? Search not into the depth of my giving birth unto God; this is most true, beyond the comprehension of human mind!

provenance.verbatim_source: Who hath heard of a childbearing Virgin, and a Mother without a husband? O Mary, thou workest a wonder! But tell me, how? Search not into the depth of my giving birth unto God; this is most true, beyond the comprehension of human mind!

items.day_or_date: On Wednesday of Palm Week, at Matins
items.english_text: Having mentally plaited palm branches of the date palms, let us visibly make a meeting for the King as He comes unto us: for blessed is He that comes in the name of the Lord and Father, as the true Son!

provenance.verbatim_source: Having mentally plaited palm branches of the date palms, let us visibly make a meeting for the King as He comes unto us: for blessed is He that comes in the name of the Lord and Father, as the true Son!

items.english_text: Israel was robed in purple and fine scarlet, shining with priestly and royal vesture, being rich in the Law and the Prophets, and rejoicing in the legal services; but having crucified outside the gates Thee, the Benefactor, Who becamest poor, and having denied Thee Who art alive after the crucifixion in the bosom of God the eternal Father: he now thirsts for a drop of grace, even as the unmerciful rich man thirsted for water from poor Lazarus; who, though once robed in purple and scarlet, hath entered into the unquenchable fire, and seeing is in anguish that the Gentile peoples, formerly destitute of even drops of truth, are now warmed in the bosom of Abraham's faith, wearing the purple robe of Thy blood with the scarlet mantle of baptism, renewed and taking delight in Thy gifts, and crying: O Christ our God, glory to Thee!

items.english_text: Neither tribulation, nor distress, nor famine, nor persecution, nor wounds, nor the fury of wild beasts, nor the sword, nor threatening fire were able to separate you, O all-lauded martyrs, from God; but rather through love for Him, having contended as though in stranger bodies, ye forgot nature, despising death; therefore worthily according to your pains ye received your reward and became inheritors of the Heavenly Kingdom; pray ye for our souls!

items.english_text: Beholding Thee hanging, O Christ, Who didst hang the earth upon the waters, O Lover of mankind, the pure one who gave Thee birth cried aloud: Woe is me! What strange sight is this? How hath Thine immeasurable beauty set, O sweetest Son? I magnify Thy mercy, for of Thine own will Thou sufferest for all!

items.english_text: Thus saith the Lord: Cry aloud with strength, and spare not; lift up thy voice like a trumpet, and declare unto My people their sins, and to the house of Jacob their iniquities. They seek Me day by day, and desire to know My ways, as a people that had done righteousness, and had not forsaken the judgment of their God; they ask of Me now righteous judgment, and desire to draw near to God, saying: Why have we fasted, and Thou sawest not? Why have we humbled our souls, and Thou tookest no knowledge? For in the days of your fasts ye find your own pleasures, and afflict all that are under your hand. If ye fast for strifes and debates, and strike the humble with fists, why fast ye unto Me as today, that your voice may be heard in crying aloud? I have not chosen such a fast, nor a day for a man to humble his soul; not even if thou bow down thy neck as a ring, and spread sackcloth and ashes under thee, not even so shall ye call it an acceptable fast. Not such a fast have I chosen, saith the Lord; but loose every bond of iniquity, untie the knots of forced obligations, let the oppressed go free, and tear in pieces every unrighteous bond! Break thy bread to the hungry, and bring the poor that have no shelter into thy house; if thou seest the naked, cover him, and hide not thyself from the kinsfolk of thine own seed. Then shall thy light break forth early in the morning, and thy healing shall spring forth speedily; and thy righteousness shall go before thee, and the glory of God shall encompass thee, O man. Then shalt thou cry, and God shall hear thee, His servant; while thou art yet speaking, He shall say: Behold, I am here! If thou take away from thee the yoke, and the pointing of the hand, and the word of murmuring; and if thou give bread from thy soul to the hungry, and satisfy the afflicted soul; then shall thy light rise in obscurity, and thy darkness shall be as the noonday, and thy God shall be with thee continually.

items.english_text: Being rich in passions, I am wrapped in the deceitful garment of hypocrisy, rejoicing in the evils of intemperance, and displaying boundless pitilessness, despising my mind, which is cast down before the doors of repentance, hungering for every good thing, and sick through my negligence; but do Thou, O Lord, make me a Lazarus, poor in sins, lest in my want I fail to receive a finger moistening my aching tongue in the unquenchable fire, but establish me in the bosom of Patriarch Abraham, as Lover of mankind!

items.english_text: Walking in the flesh on the other side of the Jordan, O Jesus, Thou didst cry unto them that were with Thee: Our friend Lazarus is already dead, and is now committed unto burial; therefore I rejoice for your sakes, O My friends, that ye may know that I know all things, being unchangeable God, even though I appear as a visible man; let us go therefore to bring him to life, that death may feel its defeat and utter destruction, which I shall openly bring to pass, granting great mercy unto the world!

items.english_text: Emulating Martha and Mary, O ye faithful, let us send divine deeds as prayers unto the Lord, that coming He may raise our mind, which lies dead and insensible in the tomb of slothfulness, feeling no divine fear whatsoever, and having now no living operations, crying: Behold, O Lord, and as of old by Thine awesome presence Thou didst raise Thy friend Lazarus, O Compassionate One, so quicken us all, granting great mercy!

items.english_text: His brethren brought Joseph the gifts which they had in their hands into the house, and bowed themselves before him with their faces to the earth. And he asked them: Are ye in health? And he said unto them: Is your father, the old man of whom ye spake, in health? Is he yet alive? And they said: Thy servant our father is in health, he is yet alive; and he said: Blessed be that man of God; and they stooped down and worshiped him. And Joseph lifted up his eyes, and saw Benjamin his brother of the same mother, and said: Is this your younger brother, whom ye said ye would bring unto me? And he said: God have mercy on thee, my child. And Joseph was troubled, for his bowels yearned over his brother, and he sought to weep; and he entered into his chamber, and wept there. And he washed his face, and went out, and refrained himself. And Joseph could not refrain himself before all that stood by him, but said: Send out everyone from me; and there stood no man with Joseph, while he made himself known unto his brethren. And he wept aloud, and all the Egyptians heard, and it was heard in Pharaoh's house. And Joseph said unto his brethren: I am Joseph; doth my father yet live? And his brethren could not answer him, for they were troubled. And Joseph said unto his brethren: Come near to me; and they came near. And he said: I am Joseph your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt. Now therefore be not grieved, nor let it seem harsh unto you, that ye sold me hither: for God did send me before you for life. For these two years hath the famine been on the earth, and there are yet five years remaining, in which there shall neither be plowing nor harvest. For God sent me before you to leave you a remnant on the earth, and to nourish your great remnant. Now therefore it was not you that sent me hither, but God: and He hath made me as a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and ruler over all the land of Egypt. Haste ye therefore, and go up to my father, and say unto him: Thus saith thy son Joseph: God hath made me lord of all the land of Egypt; come down therefore unto me, and tarry not; and thou shalt dwell in the land of Goshen of Arabia, and thou shalt be near me, thou, and thy sons, and thy sons' sons, thy sheep, and thy oxen, and all that thou hast; and I will nourish thee there, for yet five years the famine shall be on the earth, lest thou perish, and thy sons, and all thy possessions. Behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my mouth that speaks unto you. Announce therefore unto my father all my glory that is in Egypt, and all that ye have seen; and haste ye, and bring down my father hither. And falling upon the neck of his brother Benjamin, he wept over him, and Benjamin wept upon his neck. And kissing all his brethren, he wept over them; and after this his brethren talked with him. And the report was carried into Pharaoh's house, saying: Joseph's brethren are come; and Pharaoh rejoiced, and his servants.[^1201]

items.english_text: Whoso keeps his mouth and his tongue, keeps his soul from trouble. The bold and arrogant and boastful man is called a pestilence; and he that remembers injuries is a transgressor. The desires of the sluggard kill him, for his hands refuse to do anything. The ungodly man desires evil desires all the day long; but the righteous shows mercy and is generous without sparing. The sacrifices of the ungodly are an abomination to the Lord, for they offer them unlawfully. A false witness shall perish, but an obedient man shall speak with preservation. An ungodly man stands impudently with his face; but the upright man himself discerns his ways. There is no wisdom, there is no courage, there is no counsel with the ungodly. The horse is prepared for the day of battle, but help is from the Lord. A good name is better than much riches, and good favor rather than silver and gold. The rich and poor meet together; the Lord hath made them both. A prudent man, seeing the wicked punished severely, is himself chastened; but the foolish pass on and suffer loss. The generation of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and riches, and glory, and life.

items.english_text: Come, all ye brethren, before the end let us draw near with a pure heart unto the compassionate God; having cast aside worldly distractions, let us take care for our souls, abhorring the pleasures of food through abstinence, and caring for almsgiving; for through it, as it is written, some have entertained angels; feeding the poor, let us feed Him Who hath nourished us with His own flesh, and let us clothe ourselves in Him Who covers Himself with light as with a garment; that having received forgiveness of sins through the prayers of the all-pure Mother of God and Virgin Mother, we may cry unto Him with compunction: O Lord, deliver us from standing on the left hand, and vouchsafe unto us a place at Thy right hand, as Thou art merciful and the Lover of mankind!

items.english_text: Thus saith the Lord: In like manner as a grape is found on the cluster, and they say: Destroy it not, for a blessing is in it; so will I do for My servant's sake, that I will not destroy them all for his sake. And I will lead forth a seed out of Jacob, and out of Judah, and he shall inherit My holy mountain; and Mine elect and My servants shall inherit it, and shall dwell there. And there shall be in the forest folds for flocks, and the valley of Achor shall be for a resting-place of herds for My people who have sought Me. But ye who have left Me, and forget My holy mountain, and prepare a table for the demon, and fill a mingled cup unto fortune: I will deliver you up to the sword, ye shall all fall by slaughter; because I called you, and ye gave no ear; I spake, and ye disobeyed; and ye did evil before Me, and chose the things wherein I delighted not. Therefore thus saith the Lord: Behold, My servants shall eat, but ye shall hunger; behold, My servants shall drink, but ye shall thirst; behold, My servants shall rejoice, but ye shall be ashamed; behold, My servants shall be glad with gladness of heart, but ye shall cry out for sorrow of your heart, and shall wail from contrition of spirit. For ye shall leave your name for a surfeit unto Mine elect, and the Lord shall slay you; but unto them that serve Me a new name shall be named, which shall be blessed upon the earth; for they shall bless the true God.

items.english_text: Israel himself rose up and all that he had, and came to the well of the oath; and offered sacrifice to the God of his father Isaac. And God spake unto Israel in a vision by night, saying: Jacob, Jacob! And he said: What is it? And He said unto him: I am the God of thy fathers; fear not to go down into Egypt, for there will I make of thee a great nation. And I will go down with thee into Egypt, and I will bring thee up at the end; and Joseph shall lay his hands upon thine eyes. And Jacob rose up from the well of the oath; and the sons of Israel took their father, and their possessions, and their wives upon the wagons which Joseph had sent to take him. And having taken their goods, and all their substance which they had gotten in the land of Canaan, Jacob and all his seed with him entered into Egypt: his sons, and his sons' sons with him; his daughters, and his daughters' daughters, and all his seed he brought into Egypt.

items.english_text: My son, if thy heart be wise, thou shalt make my heart glad also. And thy lips shall remain in words with my lips, if they be right. Let not thy heart envy sinners, but be thou in the fear of the Lord all the day long. For if thou keep these things, thou shalt have descendants, and thine expectation shall not depart. Give ear, my son, and become wise, and direct the thoughts of thy heart. Be not a winebibber, neither join thyself unto assemblies and purchase of meats; for every drunkard and whoremonger shall become poor, and every drowsy man shall be clothed with tatters and with rags. Listen, my son, unto the father who begat thee, and despise not thy mother when she is old. Acquire truth, and reject not wisdom, and instruction, and understanding. A righteous father trains well, and over a wise son his soul rejoices; let thy father and thy mother rejoice over thee, and let her that bare thee be glad. My son, give me thy heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways. For a strange house is a broken vessel, and a strange well is narrow; for this man shall perish speedily, and every transgressor shall be cut off. To whom is woe? To whom is tumult? To whom are lawsuits? To whom are bitternesses and contentions? To whom are bruises without cause? Whose eyes are livid? Are they not theirs that tarry long at wine? Are they not theirs that hunt after where banquets be? Be not drunk with wine, but converse with righteous men, and converse in public paths; for if thou cast thine eyes upon cups and flagons, afterward thou shalt go more naked than a winnowing pole. And at last he shall lie stretched out as if bitten by a serpent, and as by a horned viper venom is diffused in him. When thine eyes behold a strange woman, thy mouth shall then speak perverse things; and thou shalt lie down as in the heart of the sea, and as a pilot in a great surge. And thou shalt say: They beat me, and I felt no pain; and they mocked me, but I knew it not; when shall morning come, that I may go and seek them with whom I may meet? My son, envy not evil men, neither desire to be with them; for their heart meditats falsehoods, and their lips speak griefs. With wisdom is a house built, and with understanding is it established; with knowledge are the chambers filled with all precious and good wealth. Better is a wise man than a strong man, and a man having understanding than a great husbandman.

provenance.verbatim_source: My son, if thy heart be wise, thou shalt make my heart glad also. And thy lips shall remain in words with my lips, if they be right. Let not thy heart envy sinners, but be thou in the fear of the Lord all the day long. For if thou keep these things, thou shalt have descendants, and thine expectation shall not depart. Give ear, my son, and become wise, and direct the thoughts of thy heart. Be not a winebibber, neither join thyself unto assemblies and purchase of meats; for every drunkard and whoremonger shall become poor, and every drowsy man shall be clothed with tatters and with rags. Listen, my son, unto the father who begat thee, and despise not thy mother when she is old. Acquire truth, and reject not wisdom, and instruction, and understanding. A righteous father trains well, and over a wise son his soul rejoices; let thy father and thy mother rejoice over thee, and let her that bare thee be glad. items.english_text: Having despised divine anointings, O my soul, thou hast been overwhelmed by the wiles of the enemy, voluntarily surrendering thyself unto corruption; and having become heavy through much sin, thou hast defiled the divinely woven garment, making it unadorned for the royal wedding; but lest thou be dragged down with sin, and recline covered with the garment of passions, being held liable for retribution, and be cast out of the bridal chamber, cry aloud unto the Savior: O awesome Eye, Who didst take on what I am, and didst not abandon what Thou wast, and before the Cross wast clothed in the cloak of mockery for my sake, tear asunder my sackcloth, and clothe me in gladness, and deliver me from the outer darkness and from eternal weeping, and have mercy on me!

items.english_text: Be glad, O Jerusalem, and keep festival in it, all ye that love it; and all ye that dwell in it, rejoice together with it in joy, all ye that mourn for it; that ye may suck and be satisfied from the breast of its consolation, that having milked it out ye may delight yourselves from the entrance of its glory. For thus saith the Lord: Behold, I incline toward them like a river of peace, and like a torrent overflowing, the glory of the Gentiles; their children shall be taken upon shoulders, and consoled upon knees. Even as when a mother comforts someone, so also will I comfort you, and in Jerusalem ye shall be comforted. And ye shall see, and your heart shall rejoice, and your bones shall spring up like grass; and the hand of the Lord shall be known unto them that fear Him, and He shall threaten the disobedient. For behold, the Lord shall come like fire, and His chariots like a whirlwind, to render His vengeance with wrath, and His rebuke in a flame of fire. For by the fire of the Lord shall all the earth be judged, and all flesh by His sword: many shall be wounded by the Lord. They that purify and sanctify themselves in the gardens, and eat swine's flesh in the porches, and abominations, and mice, shall perish together, saith the Lord. And I know their works and their thought, and I am coming to gather all nations and tongues; and they shall come and behold My glory. And I will leave a sign upon them, and I will send forth those of them that are saved unto the nations, to Tarshish, and to Pul, and to Lud, and to Meshech, and to Tubal and to Greece, and to the islands afar off, who have not heard My Name, neither have seen My glory: and they shall declare My glory among the Gentiles. And they shall bring your brethren out of all nations for a gift unto the Lord, with horses, and chariots, and with litters of mules, under awnings into the holy city of Jerusalem, saith the Lord, even as if the children of Israel would bring their sacrifices to Me with psalms into the house of the Lord. And from them will I take for Myself priests and Levites, saith the Lord. For as the new heaven and the new earth which I make remain before Me, saith the Lord, so shall your seed and your name stand. And it shall come to pass from month to month, and from Sabbath to Sabbath, all flesh shall come to worship before Me in Jerusalem, saith the Lord. And they shall go forth, and see the corpses of the men that have transgressed against Me; for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be a spectacle unto all flesh.[^1239]

items.english_text: From bed and sleep Thou hast raised me up, O Lord; enlighten my mind and heart, and open my lips, that I may hymn Thee, O Holy Trinity: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God, through the Theotokos have mercy on us!

items.english_text: O consubstantial and undivided Trinity, Tri-hypostatic and co-eternal Unity, unto Thee as God we cry aloud the angelic hymn: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God! *(Add:)*

provenance.verbatim_source: O consubstantial and undivided Trinity, Tri-hypostatic and co-eternal Unity, unto Thee as God we cry aloud the angelic hymn: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God! *(Add:)*

items.english_text: Daring to glorify in Cherubic manner the unoriginate Father, the co-unoriginate Son, and the co-eternal Spirit, one Godhead, we say: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God, by the prayers of all Thy saints have mercy on us!

items.english_text: Suddenly the Judge shall come, and the deeds of each shall be laid bare; but with fear we cry at midnight: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God, through the Theotokos have mercy on us!

items.english_text: Even as the angelic ranks now in heaven, and with fear the assemblies of men upon earth, we offer the song of victory unto Thee, O Good One: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God, by the prayers of all Thy saints have mercy on us!

items.english_text: O Thou that causest light to shine upon Thy world, cleanse my soul that is in darkness from every sin: *(Add:)* and save me!

items.english_text: Putting away sluggishness like sleep, O my soul, show forth amendment unto praise before the Judge, and cry aloud with fear: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God, by the prayers of all Thy saints have mercy on us!

items.english_text: Having our hearts on high, let us emulate the angelic rank, and with fear let us fall down before the Judge, seeking after the song of victory: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God! *(Add:)*

items.english_text: Not daring to gaze upon Thee, the Cherubim fly, crying aloud with exultation the divine song of the Thrice-Holy voice; with them also we cry unto Thee: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God, by the prayers of all Thy saints have mercy on us!

items.day_or_date: On Friday of Palm Week, at Matins
items.english_text: Bent down by the multitude of our transgressions, and not daring to look up unto the height of heaven, bowing soul and body, with the Angels we cry the hymn unto Thee: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God, through the Theotokos have mercy on us!

items.day_or_date: On Friday of Palm Week, at Matins
items.english_text: Great is the abyss of my transgressions, O Savior, and grievously am I submerged by mine iniquities; reach out Thy hand unto me, as unto Peter, and save me, O God, and have mercy on me!

provenance.verbatim_source: Great is the abyss of my transgressions, O Savior, and grievously am I submerged by mine iniquities; reach out Thy hand unto me, as unto Peter, and save me, O God, and have mercy on me!

items.day_or_date: On Friday of Palm Week, at Matins
items.english_text: Seeing that in wicked thoughts and in deeds Thou hast condemned me, O Savior, grant me the thought of repentance, O God, that I may cry unto Thee: Save me, O Good Benefactor, and have mercy on me!

provenance.verbatim_source: Seeing that in wicked thoughts and in deeds Thou hast condemned me, O Savior, grant me the thought of repentance, O God, that I may cry unto Thee: Save me, O Good Benefactor, and have mercy on me!

items.day_or_date: On Friday of Palm Week, at Matins
items.english_text: Another age awaits thee, O my soul, and the Judge desires to expose thy secret and grievous deeds; remain not therefore in the things of this world, but anticipate the judgment, crying aloud unto the Judge: O God, cleanse me and save me!

provenance.verbatim_source: Another age awaits thee, O my soul, and the Judge desires to expose thy secret and grievous deeds; remain not therefore in the things of this world, but anticipate the judgment, crying aloud unto the Judge: O God, cleanse me and save me!

items.english_text: Despise me not, O my Savior, who am held fast by sinful sloth; raise up my thoughts unto repentance, and show me to be an approved laborer of Thy vineyard, granting me the reward of the eleventh hour, and great mercy!

items.english_text: In iniquities was I conceived, prodigal that I am, and I dare not look up unto the height of heaven; yet daring upon Thy love for mankind, I cry: O God, cleanse me and save me!

items.english_text: If the righteous scarcely be saved, where shall I appear, a sinner? I have not borne the burden and the heat of the day; yet number me with the laborers of the eleventh hour, O God, and save me!

items.english_text: Beholding in thee the miracle of miracles, O Full of Grace, the creation rejoices; for thou hast conceived without seed, and hast given birth ineffably unto Him Whom the ranks of Angels cannot behold: Him, O Theotokos, entreat for our souls!

items.english_text: *Martyricon, Tone 1:* With the praise of suffering and with the honor of crowns, the glorious passion-bearers have been clothed by Thee, O Lord; for by the endurance of wounds they vanquished the lawless, and by divine power received victory from heaven: by their prayers grant us, O God, Thy great mercy!

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Martyricon, Tone 1:*
With the praise of suffering and with the honor of crowns, the glorious passion-bearers have been clothed by Thee, O Lord; for by the endurance of wounds they vanquished the lawless, and by divine power received victory from heaven: by their prayers grant us, O God, Thy great mercy!

items.season_or_tone: LENTEN OKTOECHOS SUPPLEMENT: TRINITY HYMNS AND COMPUNCTIVE STICHERA
items.day_or_date: On Friday of Palm Week, at Matins
items.slavonic_text: Ѡ҆б̾ѧ́тїѧ Ѻ́ч҃а ѿве́рзети ми пощи́сѧ, блꙋ́днѣ моѐ и҆ждѝхъ житїѐ, на бога́тство неиждива́емое взира́ѧй щедро́тъ твои́хъ Сп҃се: ны́нѣ ѡ҆бнища́вшее не пре́зри се́рдце, тебѣ́ бо Гдⷭ҇и, оумиле́нїемъ зовꙋ̀: согрѣши́хъ на нб҃о и҆ пред̾ тобо́ю.
items.english_text: Haste Thou to open Thy Fatherly embrace unto me, for prodigally have I spent my life, looking upon the inexhaustible wealth of Thy compassions, O Savior; despise not now my heart grown poor, for unto Thee, O Lord, in compunction do I cry: I have sinned against heaven and before Thee!

provenance.verbatim_source: Haste Thou to open Thy Fatherly embrace unto me, for prodigally have I spent my life, looking upon the inexhaustible wealth of Thy compassions, O Savior; despise not now my heart grown poor, for unto Thee, O Lord, in compunction do I cry: I have sinned against heaven and before Thee!

items.slavonic_text: Стї́хъ: Гдⷭ҇и, да не ꙗ҆́ростїю твое́ю ѡ҆бличи́ши менѐ, нижѐ гнѣ́вомъ твои́мъ нака́жеши менѐ.
items.english_text: *Verse: O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger, nor chasten me in Thy wrath.*[^1246]

provenance.verbatim_source: *Verse: O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger, nor chasten me in Thy wrath.*[^1246]

items.slavonic_text: Сꙋди́ще твоѐ стра́шное, и҆ сꙋ́дъ пра́веденъ, дѣла̀ моѧ̑ лю̑та: но са́мъ Ми́лостиве, предвари́въ мѧ̀ спасѝ, и҆ мꙋ́ки свободѝ, и҆зба́ви Влдко ѿ ко́злищъ ча́сти, и҆ сподо́би мѧ̀ ѡ҆деснꙋ́ю тебѐ ста́ти, Сꙋдїѐ пра́веднѣйшїй.
items.english_text: Thy judgment seat is fearful, and Thy judgment is just, and my deeds are grievous; but do Thou Thyself, O Merciful One, anticipate and save me, and deliver me from torment; rescue me, O Master, from the portion of the goats, and count me worthy to stand at Thy right hand, O most righteous Judge!

provenance.verbatim_source: Thy judgment seat is fearful, and Thy judgment is just, and my deeds are grievous; but do Thou Thyself, O Merciful One, anticipate and save me, and deliver me from torment; rescue me, O Master, from the portion of the goats, and count me worthy to stand at Thy right hand, O most righteous Judge!

items.day_or_date: On Friday of Palm Week, at Matins
items.slavonic_text: Заче́нши неѡпа́льнѡ Ѻ́гнь Бж҃ества̀, и҆ ро́ждши безсѣ́меннѡ и҆сто́чника живота̀ Гдⷭ҇а, благода́тнаѧ Бцⷣе, спаса́й тѧ̀ велича́ющыѧ.
items.english_text: Having conceived without being consumed the Fire of the Godhead, and having given birth without seed unto the Lord, the Fountain of life: O Full of Grace, Theotokos, save those who magnify thee!

provenance.verbatim_source: Having conceived without being consumed the Fire of the Godhead, and having given birth without seed unto the Lord, the Fountain of life: O Full of Grace, Theotokos, save those who magnify thee!

items.slavonic_text: Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́брїи во́ини, є҆диномꙋ́дреннѡ вѣ́ровавше, преще́нїѧ мꙋчи́телей не оу҆боѧ́вшесѧ ст҃і́и, пристꙋпи́сте ᲂу҆се́рднѡ ко Хрⷭ҇тꙋ̀, взе́мше чтⷭ҇ны́й крⷭ҇тъ, и҆ сконча́вше тече́нїе, съ нб҃ѐ побѣ́дꙋ прїѧ́сте, сла́ва ᲂу҆крѣ́пльшемꙋ ва́съ, сла́ва вѣнча́вшемꙋ ва́съ, сла́ва дѣ́йствꙋющемꙋ ва́ми всѣ̑мъ и҆сцѣле́нїѧ.
items.english_text: As noble soldiers, of one mind having believed, not having feared the threats of the tyrants, O holy ones, ye approached eagerly unto Christ, taking up the precious Cross, and having finished your course, ye received victory from heaven: glory to Him Who strengthened you; glory to Him Who crowned you; glory to Him Who through you works healings for all!

provenance.verbatim_source: As noble soldiers, of one mind having believed, not having feared the threats of the tyrants, O holy ones, ye approached eagerly unto Christ, taking up the precious Cross, and having finished your course, ye received victory from heaven: glory to Him Who strengthened you; glory to Him Who crowned you; glory to Him Who through you works healings for all!

items.day_or_date: On Friday of Palm Week, at Matins
items.slavonic_text: Ѻ҆рꙋ́жїе крⷭ҇тное во бранѣ́хъ, ꙗ҆ви́сѧ нѣ́когда бл҃гочести́вомꙋ царю̀ Кѡнстанти́нꙋ, непобѣди́маѧ побѣ́да на врагѝ вѣ́ры ра́ди, сегѡ̀ трепе́щꙋтъ сопроти́вныѧ си́лы: се́й бы́сть вѣ́рнымъ спасенїе, и҆ Па́влꙋ похвала̀.
items.english_text: The weapon of the Cross in battles was shown forth of old unto the pious Emperor Constantine as an invincible victory over enemies for the sake of the faith, at which the adverse powers tremble; this has become salvation unto the faithful, and the boast of Paul.

provenance.verbatim_source: The weapon of the Cross in battles was shown forth of old unto the pious Emperor Constantine as an invincible victory over enemies for the sake of the faith, at which the adverse powers tremble; this has become salvation unto the faithful, and the boast of Paul.

items.day_or_date: On Friday of Palm Week, at Matins
items.slavonic_text: Стї́хъ: Возноси́те Гдⷭ҇а Бг҃а на́шего, и҆ покланѧ́йтесѧ подно́жїю нѡ́гꙋ є҆гѡ̀, ꙗ҆́кѡ ст҃о є҆́сть.
items.english_text: *Verse: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship the footstool of His feet, for He is holy.*[^1247]

provenance.verbatim_source: *Verse: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship the footstool of His feet, for He is holy.*[^1247]
